h: Personal Sanctification and the Renewal of the Oral Torah

p: Behold, the order of the topics
the matter of the resting of the Shechinah
through the completion of the three camps:
for through the fixing of the places
of the camp of Yisrael and the camp of the Levi'im,
וִישַׁלְּחוּ מִן הַמַּחֲנֶה וְגוֹ׳ (בְּמִדְבַּר ה, ב)
"They shall send out of the camp," etc. (Bamidbar 5:2),
even after holiness has come to rest in the soul;
and as it says in the Midrash,
that precisely after the giving of the Torah
the impurity of zivah and tzaraas,
so that one must be sent out
from the camp of the Shechinah.
a person may fall in spirit
thinking, God forbid, that there is no hope.
the parshah of robbing a convert,
in which it says "and he shall confess" (Bamidbar 5:7),
that there is a remedy for everything
as it says in the Ra'aya Mehemna on this parshah
And the Rambam, of blessed memory, too,
counted the positive mitzvah of teshuvah
After this comes the parshah of the sotah:
that a person should not be afraid in his heart
if a stumbling block occurred before him
something he had no ability to guard against,
like a woman secluding herself with another man
there is counsel according to the Torah
for the sin to be clarified,
After this comes the parshah of the nazir,
"sanctify yourself in what is permitted to you" (Yevamos 20a),
"One who sees a sotah in her disgrace
and especially in the days of youth,
"And I raised up of your young men as nezirim";
And there is great depth in this matter,
for sometimes he is not permitted,
and he is called a sinner,
that a nazir is a sinner,
for he afflicted himself by abstaining from wine;
(Yerushalmi, cited in the Ran there, Nedarim 22b):
"Is it not enough for you what the Torah forbade,
However, one who feels within himself
like the nazir of Shimon HaTzaddik
who take the vow of nezirus, in Yisrael"
one from the sense of wondrous and hidden;
"Nezirus was given only for explicit declaration,"
and "a minor who knows how to declare explicitly."
along the lines of what our Sages, of blessed memory, said
"Behold, I will again do wonders," etc.,
הַפְלָאָה זוֹ אֵינִי יוֹדֵעַ מָה הוּא
"This wonder, I do not know what it is;
'and the wisdom of its wise men shall be lost,' etc.,
say then that it speaks of the wonder of Torah."
That is the meaning of the doubled phrase
that there will be hidden and concealed
of the wisdom of the Torah.
both of the meanings mentioned above,
that is, that there will be revealed and explicit before him
of the power of the wisdom of the Torah.
For when a person feels in his soul
that he needs to place a fence on himself
הוּא בָּא עַל עוֹמֶק דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה
he arrives at the depth of the words of Torah
for he did a wondrous thing in this.
And with this will be understood the law
that if a person accepts upon himself
that it should be upon him
on what he forbade upon himself
However, the substance of the matter is this:
in the Sanhedrin and the sages of the generations
to make a fence and a safeguard
שֶׁלֹּא יוֹעִיל עַל זֶה שׁוּם הַתָּרָה
for this is the essential power
and just as in every city
the leaders of the city have the power
when he sees in his soul
יֵשׁ לוֹ כֹּחַ כְּמוֹ אִיסּוּר שֶׁל תּוֹרָה
it has the force of a Torah prohibition;
and consequently, when he says so,
and consequently he has no annulment.
in the words "A man who sets himself apart":
that is, when he sees within himself
then he arrives at the wonder of wisdom
And the matter of the parshah of the nazir
מְרַמֵּז עַל כֹּחַ תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
alludes to the power of the Oral Torah,
for this is the essential power of the Sages
for the needs of the hour,
and they have force like the body of the Torah.

paragraphs.text: Source: Shoftim 13:19 — “ויקח מנוח את גדי העזים ואת המנחה ויעל על הצור ליהוה ומפלא לעשות ומנוח ואשתו ראים” — “Manoah took the kid and the grain offering and offered them up on the rock to GOD; and a marvelous thing happened while Manoah and his wife looked on.”

p: After this is stated Birkas Kohanim,
the blessing of the flow of the power of Torah,
as we have spoken of it.
the offerings of the dedication by the Nesi'im,
to the very power of innovation
what a person innovates from his heart;
devised on his own, from his heart,
to bring this number of offerings,
as it says in the Midrash
that all of them brought of their own accord
all their offering on the first day,
the number of offerings and their meal offerings
and the weight of the vessels,
although all of them offered equally,
like the number of the first,"
and so for all of them.
From this the Midrash Rabbah proves
had different intentions in his offering;
perform a deed in one form,
עִם כָּל זֶה יֵשׁ לְכָל אֶחָד
a matter and a level of his own,
according to the measure of his heart's preparation
in the inner dimension of the matter;
And just as there are differences
each one sensing a different flavor
so too there is a difference in time:
the intention of the mitzvah is not alike
from one day to the next,
even in that very same mitzvah.
in the name of the tzaddikim of the generation,
that all the kavanos of the Arizal in prayer
and one whose soul is refined
and taste a different intention in his prayer.
And this is like the matter of
that was created in the six days of work
is renewed in all the six days of the week,
even though "there is nothing new under the sun"
rather, to that very same thing
מִכֹּחַ שֵׁשֶׁת יְמֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה שֶׁל הַבְּרִיאָה
from the power of the six days of Creation.
the Holy One, blessed be He,

— “Only that shall happen That has happened,Only that occur That has occurred;There is nothing new Beneath the sun!”

p: Now after there were spelled out individually
all the offerings of the Nesi'im,
the total of all of them together,
yet a separate parshah was written about it
to teach us through this as well
that just as there is an intention
even in that very same deed,
through the combining of the total
just as on each day individually there is
from the six days of Creation,
one senses the flavor of renewal
of the six days of Creation together,
"And the heavens and the earth were completed," etc.,
"And God completed on the seventh day," etc.;
"The most desirable of days You called it."
And this is the essence of the desirability and endearment
in that the Idra is mentioned
in the holy Zohar in this parshah,
הֱבִיאַנִי הַמֶּלֶךְ חֲדָרָיו (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים א, ד)
"The King has brought me into His chambers" (Shir HaShirim 1:4),
into the chambers of the Oral Torah;
in the words of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai:
אֲנָן בַּחֲבִיבוּתָא תַּלְיָא מִילְּתָא (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג קכח, א)
"With us, the matter depends on love" (Zohar III 128a),
